showName: Little Gransden Air and Car Show
title: Trains to St Neots
from: stations on Thameslink and the East Coast Main Line
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Little Gransden Air and Car Show. St Neots is the nearest station, on the Thameslink line between London, Stevenage and Peterborough. It’s about 6 miles from the airfield and there’s no show shuttle, so the last bit is a taxi. I’ve added the trains that work well on a Sunday from London, Gatwick, Brighton, Cambridge, Norwich and further up the East Coast Main Line. If you’re starting on the c2c line, from Shoeburyness, Southend, Basildon, Grays or anywhere along to Barking, I’ve added those stations too, with the change in London. Pick your station and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for Little Gransden. There’s no shuttle, so book your taxi from here before the day. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: There’s no show shuttle from St Neots, so I would book a taxi before the day. The airfield is about 6 miles away and the taxi takes about 15 to 20 minutes. There’s no useful Sunday bus, and walking isn’t practical.
walkBack: Rural taxis are limited on show days, so I would agree a pick up time with your taxi before the flying ends, and allow for traffic leaving the airfield.
tip: Rural taxis are limited on show days, so I would book both journeys before the day.
I would check your train home before you travel and book your return taxi to match. Sunday trains can be quieter, and engineering works are common on a Sunday.
The gates opened at 10:00 in 2026, with flying from about 12:30, which gives you time to walk the lines of cars before the display starts.

note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows journeys from the main stations and city termini around the UK to St Neots, with the changes that work well. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 2 November 2026, so they are a guide to how Sunday trains run rather than the show day times. The big stations and city termini further from St Neots use the times for Sunday 15 November 2026, checked on 10 November 2026. The summer 2027 times will follow, so please check before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: Thameslink, plus the trains that connect well. Thameslink stops at St Neots on its way between London and Peterborough, and I’ve added Great Northern and the other companies where the change works on a Sunday. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there. I’ve also added eight c2c stations, with the c2c train into London and the connection on from there.

pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. With a taxi to match, a flexible ticket home can take the stress out of it.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you don’t know when you’ll want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.
A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: St Neots. It’s the nearest station, about 6 miles from the airfield, and a taxi takes about 15 to 20 minutes.
No. There’s no show shuttle and no useful Sunday bus, so I would book a taxi both ways before the day. Walking isn’t practical.
Are there other stations I could use?

Sandy is also on the Thameslink line from London, about 8 miles from the airfield, so I would take a taxi from there too. Cambridge has the most trains, but it’s about 15 miles away and a taxi takes around 30 minutes. That may work for you if you’re coming from Norwich, Ipswich, Birmingham or Stansted Airport.
Do I need a ticket for the show?
Yes. Tickets are online through the official site, and every ticket helps children’s charities.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station, and let your taxi firm know.
access: Trains can work really well for a show, as long as you plan the step free parts and the taxi before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
If you need a wheelchair accessible taxi, I would book it well before the day, as rural firms only have a few.
